label: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation / Stretch Extinction Using Counterflow Flames
title: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation / Stretch Extinction Using Counterflow Flames
tier_reason: Team list, Tier 1. Ground study; PSI subarea: Spacecraft Fire Safety. Uses FLEX flight data.

summary_student.text: This ground study used data from the FLEX experiment, where fuel droplets burned on the International Space Station, plus computer models and lab flames. It looked at when an ordinary hot flame turns into a weak 'cool flame', and how much oxygen, pressure and mixing it takes for each kind of flame to keep burning. Knowing these burning limits matters for spacecraft fire safety.

summary_professional.text: Ground investigation using FLEX flight conditions and data to study oxygen-concentration effects on cool-flame extinction limits with three numerical schemes: spark-assisted flame propagation of n-heptane/air, one-dimensional freely-propagating dimethyl ether (DME) flames with arc-length continuation, and DME/air cool flame regimes and burning limits at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm). Ground experiments used ozone-sensitized counterflow flames to map flammability limits of diffusional cool flames affected by radiation, diffusion and convection. Measured or computed quantities were extinction limits, flame temperature and species distribution for validating kinetic and radiation models.

pillar.reason: Its PSI subarea is Spacecraft Fire Safety, and it develops a flammability-limit diagram for cool flames and links it to hot-flame flammability and extinction limits, which describes when a fuel can keep burning.
